sourceBrief.prompt: Pendulums are in common usage. Some have crucial uses, such as in clocks; some are for fun, such as a child's swing; and some are just there, such as the sinker on a fishing line. For small displacements, a pendulum is a simple harmonic oscillator. A simple pendulum is defined to have an object that has a small mass, also known as the pendulum bob, which is suspended from a light wire or string.

beats.title: A simple pendulum
beats.narration: A small mass — the bob — on a light string, free to swing. For small displacements it is a simple harmonic oscillator.

beats.title: Crucial uses: the clock
beats.narration: A swinging pendulum keeps a clock's time — its period depends only on length and gravity, not on how hard it swings.

beats.title: For fun: the swing
beats.narration: A child's swing is a pendulum you can ride — same physics, human scale.

beats.title: Just there: the sinker
beats.narration: Even a fishing sinker hanging on a line is a pendulum.

beats.title: All the same idea
beats.narration: Clock, swing, sinker — all pendulums, all swinging to the same simple law.
